title: Ext out of a constructible sheaf commutes with sums of ind-constructible sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian ([pqf-def-locnoeth]) and quasi-compact ([def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, with coefficient ring object $\Lambda_X$ as in [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring] or [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring], respectively. Write $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ for the category of module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]), and $D(\mathcal A)$ for its unbounded derived category ([def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). Let $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ denote the full subcategory of constructible module sheaves ([sk-def-sfb-constructible]), and let $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ denote the full subcategory of small filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$.

For $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, $q\in\mathbf Z$, and a family $(B_s)_{s\in S}$ in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ indexed by a set $S$, define $\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B)=\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}(C,B[q])$, with sheaves placed in degree zero. The natural map induced by the coprojections $B_s\to\bigoplus_{s\in S}B_s$,

$$
\bigoplus_{s\in S}\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_s)\longrightarrow\Ext^q_\Lambda\Bigl(C,\bigoplus_{s\in S}B_s\Bigr),
$$

is an isomorphism. The sum on the left is in abelian groups and the sum on the right is in $\mathcal A$.

proof.text: View $\mathcal A$ as sheaves of modules over the commutative ring sheaf $\Lambda_X$: the tensor-action definition [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is the same compatible module structure on sections. The site is small in the chosen universe, so [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] supplies the abelian category and its small coproducts and colimits. For a finite subset $T\subseteq S$, put $B_T=\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s$. Its inclusions $\iota_{s,T}$ and projections $\pi_{s,T}$ satisfy $\pi_{t,T}\iota_{s,T}=\delta_{s,t}$ and $\sum_{s\in T}\iota_{s,T}\pi_{s,T}=1$. These identities hold termwise for degree-zero complexes and persist under the additive localization to $D(\mathcal A)$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The shift is an additive automorphism by [def-weil-triangulated-category], so the identities also hold after shifting by $q$. Thus the map $\Phi_T:(f_s)\mapsto\sum_{s\in T}\iota_{s,T}[q]\circ f_s$ from $\bigoplus_{s\in T}\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_s)$ to $\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_T)$ has inverse $h\mapsto(\pi_{s,T}[q]\circ h)_s$, by the two displayed identities. For $T=\varnothing$ both groups are zero. For $T\subseteq U$ the map $j_{T,U}:B_T\to B_U$ satisfies $j_{T,U}\iota_{s,T}=\iota_{s,U}$, so $\Phi_U$ composed with zero-extension of tuples equals $\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,j_{T,U})\Phi_T$. Hence the $\Phi_T$ form an isomorphism of diagrams, for every integer $q$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; ambient module category from Stacks Tags 03DA (sites-modules-lemma-abelian) and 03DB (sites-modules-lemma-limits-colimits)

proof.text: The poset $\operatorname{Fin}(S)$ of finite subsets is nonempty (it contains $\varnothing$), and $T\cup U$ is an upper bound for $T,U$, so it is filtered. Since $S$ is a set in the chosen universe, this poset is small. In any category with the coproducts under consideration, a compatible family of maps $\bigoplus_{s\in T}A_s\to Z$ is uniquely determined by its maps $A_s\to Z$ at $T=\{s\}$: compatibility forces each map at $T$ to be the coproduct of those maps. Conversely any family $A_s\to Z$ supplies these compatible maps. This is exactly the universal property of $\bigoplus_{s\in S}A_s$, and proves $\varinjlim_T\bigoplus_{s\in T}A_s\cong\bigoplus_{s\in S}A_s$. The required colimits and coproducts of $\mathcal A$ exist by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]; in abelian groups they are the usual direct limits and direct sums. Apply this argument in $\mathcal A$ to $A_s=B_s$ and in abelian groups to $A_s=\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_s)$. For empty $S$ the diagram has the single object $T=\varnothing$ and the conclusion is still valid. This argument uses categorical coproducts and does not identify sheaf coproducts with sectionwise direct sums.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: finite-subset colimit identifications

proof.text: Place each $B_T$ in degree zero; these complexes all vanish below the common degree $0$. The constructible-sheaf clause of [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity] applies on the given Noetherian scheme $X$ to the filtered diagram indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(S)$, to the given constructible $C$, and to $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. It gives the isomorphism $\gamma:\varinjlim_T\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_T)\to\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,\varinjlim_T B_T)$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$. Use Step 2 to identify its target with $\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,\bigoplus_SB_s)$. Step 1 gives an isomorphism on colimits, since its compatible inverse maps also induce inverse maps on colimits; Step 2 identifies its source with $\bigoplus_S\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_s)$. For $f\in\Ext^q_\Lambda(C,B_s)$, the resulting composite is represented at $T=\{s\}$ and maps to $\iota_s[q]\circ f$, where $\iota_s:B_s\to\bigoplus_SB_s$. The composite therefore agrees on each summand with the stated natural map, and is an isomorphism.

statement_change.what: The blueprint leaves X unbound and states no global Noetherian convention. Its unrestricted reading is false in degree zero on a countable disjoint union of algebraically closed points. Add the Noetherian scope already required by the cited constructible Ext-continuity lemma, and bind the coefficient ring objects, ordinary derived category, IndCons and Ext explicitly; preserve both coefficient choices and every integer degree.

statement_change.counterexample: Take X = coproduct over n in N of Spec(k), k algebraically closed of characteristic different from ell; C = E_X and B_n its regular module on component n and zero elsewhere. All are affine-locally constructible. Their coproduct is C componentwise. Every finite sum of maps C -> B_n vanishes off finitely many components, whereas id_C is nonzero on every component. Therefore the degree-zero comparison is not surjective.

citers.note: Its separated finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian, by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian applied to Spec(k), and its Step 3 uses exactly the preserved all-integer Ext-sum comparison.

old_proof.text:
For a finite subset $T\subset S$, the map $\bigoplus_{s\in T}\Ext^q(C,B_s)\to\Ext^q(C,\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s)$
is an isomorphism because $\Ext^q(C,-)=\Hom(C,-[q])$ is additive and finite direct sums are biproducts.
The sum $\bigoplus_{s\in S}B_s$ is the filtered colimit, over the finite subsets $T$ ordered by
inclusion, of the sheaves $\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s$ in degree $0$. By part (1) of
[sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity],

$$
\Ext^q\Bigl(C,\bigoplus_SB_s\Bigr)=\varinjlim_T\Ext^q\Bigl(C,\bigoplus_TB_s\Bigr)
=\varinjlim_T\bigoplus_T\Ext^q(C,B_s)=\bigoplus_S\Ext^q(C,B_s),
$$

and the composite is the natural map.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-b7ec4f012 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the whole item and every cited node's statement, the blueprint sk-cor-ind-heart-ii-sums(.proof).md, the unit and chapter records, and the continuity blueprint. The added Noetherian hypothesis is a correctly documented E7 source error. The chapter puts no condition on X, and the counterexample checks out: on X = countable disjoint union of Spec k, E_X is the sum of its component pieces B_n, all constructible under the affine-local definition, and id_{E_X} is not a finite sum of maps C -> B_n, so the degree-0 map is not surjective. The fix takes exactly the Noetherian scope of the cited sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity and matches the sibling det-ind-heart-ii-vanishing. It keeps both coefficient choices and all q, and the item is not a target. The only citer, det-constructible-compactness-bounded (separated finite type over a field, hence Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, Step 3 with q=s-a), still holds. The coefficient rings p_X^*E and p_X^*Qlb, the Mod_{Λ_X} module objects, the ordinary unbounded D and Cons are the same as in the continuity lemma. Step 1: finite biproduct identities survive the additive localization and the shift; the empty set case is covered. Step 2: Fin(S) is small and filtered, and the colimit equals the categorical coproduct with no sectionwise claim. Step 3: all hypotheses of the continuity lemma are supplied (Noetherian X, constructible C, common lower degree 0, termwise colimit = coproduct), and the composite is the natural map. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses, and there is no cycle. No new nodes. The rg duplicate search over IndCons and sum nodes found no duplicate.
